newsitem.title: TURKEY: ID checks can hurt cash for banned Turk groups.
newsitem.headline: ID checks can hurt cash for banned Turk groups.

text.p: Making it obligatory to produce proof of identity when making money transfers to Turkey from European countries would help cut off funds to illegal rebel Kurdish and radical Islamist groups, Turkish bankers said on Friday.

"If we make identifying yourself obligatory for transfers of more than a certain amount of money, it will have a deterrent effect on the use of legal channels by illegal organisations," general manager of a major Turkish bank told Reuters.

Turkish generals told a press briefing on Tuesday that separatist and Islamist groups in Turkey received two billion dollars of "dirty money" every year and some of this was transfered through Turkish banks.
The bankers said it was impossible to pick out money sent to illegal groups from among transfers to the country from the Turkish workers living abroad, which stand at around $4 billion annually.
"We cannot call this money laundering, it is just a sort of transfer and we cannot blame the banking system," the general manager said.
Most of the money transfers to Turkey are made from Germany.
The banker said Turkish banks and the German government had a few months ago made IDs compulsory for the transfers of more than 20,000 DM, following a series of meetings and studies.
"We are ready to lower the limit to 10,000 DM," he said.
The general manager of another private bank said identification checks should also be made obligatory in Turkey for money transfers for broader control of illegal groups' financial activities.
"The limit to report identities in money transfers to the central bank is currently $50,000. This should be reduced sharply," he told Reuters.
"Making identity checks at every phase of money transfers through separate banks would also very much increase supervision," he added.
